commits.message:
Merge pull request #6 from GSA-SHARE-IT/DSACMS/index-schema-update

Schemas: Add proposed agency-index.json v1.0.0 schema
commits.author: Natalia Luzuriaga

items: `identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`$id` updated to `https://gsa-share-it.github.io/code-json-schema.json` (reflecting the repository's move from the `DSACMS` org to `GSA-SHARE-IT`).
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
`identifier` added to `required`.
`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, `date`, `description`, `laborHours`, `languages`, `tags`, and `vcs` removed from `required` (now optional).
`feedbackMechanism` (singular)

`version`, `homepageURL`, `downloadURL`, `disclaimerURL`, `disclaimerText`, `relatedCode`, `reusedCode`, `partners` added as optional fields, taken from original [M-16-21 code.json schema](https://github.com/GSA/code-gov-data/tree/master/schemas)
`AIUseCaseID` added for assisting with agency collection of their AI Use Case Inventory as part of M-25-21 compliance
`SBOM` added to include software's SBOM in metadata as part of EO 14028

`categories`, `feedbackMechanisms` (plural, replaced by singular `feedbackMechanism`), `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, `softwareType` — these agency-extension-style fields were dropped from the generic gov-wide schema.
Migrated `$schema` dialect from `draft-04` to `2020-12` and introduced a formal `$id` (`https://dsacms.github.io/code-json-schema.json`).

Corrected the same structural bug present in `gov-schema-1.0.0.json`, where all field definitions were incorrectly nested one level too deep under a top-level `items` key instead of directly under `properties`.
`permissions.usageType` changed from a single `string` value to an `array` of strings, allowing multiple exemption reasons to be declared simultaneously.

Expanded and refined the exemption enum taxonomy: the old `exemptByLaw` was split into `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByNationalIntelligence`, `exemptByFOIA`, `exemptByEAR`, `exemptByITAR`, `exemptByTSA`, and `exemptByClassifiedInformation`; the old `exemptByNationalSecurity` (covering national security, confidentiality, _and_ individual privacy risk) was split so privacy risk became its own value, `exemptByPrivacyRisk`; `exemptByIPRestriction` was also added.

`organization`: removed the CMS-specific enum restriction (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`) and generalized it to a free-text string with an example (`'18F'` or `'Navy'`) suitable for any agency.
Top-level `additionalProperties` changed from `false` to `true`, allowing agencies to extend the schema with their own custom fields.

`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, and `feedbackMechanism` added to `required`; `categories`, `feedbackMechanisms`, `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, and `softwareType` removed from `required` (dropped entirely, see Removed above).
Field definitions are nested one level too deep under `properties.items` instead of directly under `properties` (the same structural bug present in the CMS schema's `schema-0.0.0.json`).

`permissions.usageType` is a single `string` value (not an array), so only one exemption reason could be declared per release, with a smaller 8-value exemption enum (`openSource`, `governmentWideReuse`, `exemptByLaw`, `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, `exemptByPolicyDate`).
`organization` was restricted to a CMS-only enum value (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`), despite this being the generic, agency-agnostic schema.
`identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
Updated the `usageType` description text to define and renumber all 13 enum values to match.

Reworded the `reuseFrequency` description for clarity: _"Measures frequency of code reuse in various forms such as forks and clones for repositories, and downloads for packaged and distributed software."_

fix(misc#350): narrow the GitHub OIDC deploy role trust per account (#651)

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#350

This is the first stage of scoping down the shared GitHub OIDC role,
`ztmf_github_actions`. It narrows who can assume the role. It does not
change what the role can do yet.

The role exists in both the dev and prod accounts. Both trusted
`repo:CMS-Enterprise/ztmf:*` and `repo:CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui:*` with
AdministratorAccess attached, so any branch, tag or PR run in either
repo that reached a `ROLEARN` secret could assume admin in prod.

## What changes

- **Prod account:** only jobs in the `PROD` (ztmf) and `prod` (ztmf-ui)
environments can assume the role.
- **Dev account:** jobs in the `DEV`/`IMPL` and `dev`/`impl`
environments, plus the per-PR environment workflows that share this role
through `PR_ENV_ROLEARN`. Those are `pull_request` (build, teardown,
publish-main), `pr-ztmf-*` and `pr-ui-*` (deploy), and
`ref:refs/heads/main` (the scheduled reaper).
- The `aud` and `sub` conditions use `StringEquals` and `StringLike`
instead of `ForAllValues:` and `ForAnyValue:`. Both claims hold a single
value, and `ForAllValues` also matches when the key is missing from the
token.

I took every subject from the workflows in both repos, on `main` and on
`impl`. Both repos use GitHub's default subject template.

**Behavior change:** dispatching the reaper from a branch other than
main now fails at "AWS - Get Credentials".

## Not in this PR

- A separate least-privilege role for the per-PR environment workflows
and the reaper. After that, the dev role can drop the `pull_request`,
`pr-*` and `main` subjects.
- Replacing AdministratorAccess with a scoped policy. The main root
manages IAM, including this role, so that policy needs a plan and an
apply in dev to verify.
- After this change, the prod trust rests on the `PROD`/`prod`
environment name, and neither environment has required reviewers or a
branch limit.
[ztmf-misc#459](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/459)
covers that.

## Verification

- `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass. I rendered the
trust policy JSON for dev and prod: dev gets the nine subjects and prod
gets exactly the two.
- A separate review listed every job in both repos that assumes the
role, worked out its subject, and checked it against the policy for the
account it deploys to. Every one is still allowed. The merge run applies
this through Infrastructure DEV and then Infrastructure PROD, and both
stay allowed, so the apply cannot lock itself out.

## Before merging

- Please confirm that the `PROD`/`prod` `ROLEARN` secrets point at the
prod account's role, that `DEV`/`IMPL`/`dev`/`impl` point at dev's role,
and that `PR_ENV_ROLEARN` in both repos is dev's `ztmf_github_actions`
ARN. I could not read the secret values.
- If someone with console access can list the distinct `sub` values on
`AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` events for this role in CloudTrail over the
last 90 days, in both accounts, that would catch a caller outside these
two repos' workflows.

## After merge

Watch the DEV and PROD jobs of the merge run, the next ztmf-ui merge,
the next PR environment build and deploy, and the 07:00 UTC reaper. A
missed subject fails at "Get AWS Creds" before Terraform runs, so
nothing is left half applied. If prod is locked out, the fix is to
revert this change and apply the revert from a workstation with prod
credentials.

fix(misc#421): stop the pr-env reaper when an AWS list call fails (#648)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#421

## What

`scripts/pr-env-reaper.sh` builds its two lists from AWS at the top of
the run: the `pr/` state keys from S3 and the `pr-*` services from ECS.
Each list was one pipeline that ended in `grep ... || true`. Under
`pipefail`, a failed AWS call failed the pipeline, and the `|| true`
turned that into an empty list. The run then went on as if there were no
state keys or no services.

That empty list is wrong in a costly way. With no state keys, step 2
reports every running `pr-*` service as an orphan to clean up by hand.
With no services, step 1 reports every open environment as a partial
deploy. Both land in the tracking issue as work for a person.

This PR:

- Runs each AWS call on its own and checks its exit status. If either
call fails, the script prints a `::error::` that names the call and
exits 1. This happens before any environment is checked or reaped.
- Removes the `2>/dev/null` on the S3 call, so the AWS error text shows
up in the job log.
- Keeps `|| true` on the `grep` only. No match there is a valid empty
set.
- Adds a small `fail` helper next to `log` and `finding` for the
`::error::` and exit.

The workflow needs no change. Its Report step already runs on failure,
touches `findings.md`, and writes "the reaper run failed" when the job
status is not success. Since the script exits before writing its report,
no findings go out with that message.

## One more instance of the same pattern

Step 3 lists GitHub Environments with `gh api ... | grep ... || true`,
the same shape. A failed call there skipped the check in silence. It did
not produce false findings, so it was not as bad. I fixed it in the same
way, with one difference: a failed list there adds a finding and moves
on to the next repo instead of exiting. Step 3 runs after steps 1 and 2
may have reaped environments and recorded findings, and exiting would
throw those findings away. The finding still puts the failure in the
tracking issue.

## How I showed it failing

There is no test setup for the scripts in this repo, so I ran the script
against stub `aws` and `gh` commands on `PATH`, with `--dry-run`, and
ran the version on `main` with the same stubs to compare.

| Case | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `s3api list-objects-v2` fails | exit 0, false orphan finding for the
running service, no AWS error in the log | exit 1, AWS error in the log,
`::error::aws s3api list-objects-v2 failed ...`, no report written |
| `ecs list-services` fails | exit 0, false partial-deploy finding for
the open PR | exit 1, `::error::aws ecs list-services failed ...`, no
report written |
| Empty `pr/` prefix (`None`), no `pr-*` services | exit 0, empty report
| same |
| Three state keys, four services, one key with no service, one service
with no key | exit 0, two findings | same output, line for line |
| `gh api` environments list fails | exit 0, step 3 skipped with no
finding | exit 0, one finding per repo whose list failed |

I also ran the workflow's Report step by hand after the failed S3 case.
It wrote only the "run failed" line, with no findings.

shellcheck 0.11.0 is clean on the script.

## Out of scope

- If the script exits partway through for any other reason, such as a
`gh api` error while reading a PR in step 1, the findings it already
recorded are lost because the report is only written at the end. That is
older behavior, and this PR does not change it.
- `retire_github_env` reads the deployment IDs in a `for ... in $(gh api
...)` list, so a failed read skips marking deployments inactive and goes
straight to deleting the environment. Low impact, left as is.
- Step 3 asks for 100 environments per repo and does not page. That is
fine at today's counts.
- The token preflight is
[ztmf-misc#420](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/420),
and it is separate from this change. Both are part of
[ztmf-misc#419](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/419).
The reaper itself came in with
[ztmf!601](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/601).

commits.message:
fix(ztmf#645): apply reduced pillar scope in the rollover and Compare Data Calls (#646)

Refs #645. The data call rollover no longer copies answers on pillars
the reduced pillar scope rule (#545) hides for the system in the new
call, and Compare Data Calls applies the same rule so those hidden rows
never show up as changes. This is the code half of #645; the one-off
cleanup of rows already copied into the current cycle runs separately,
after this merges.

### Why it happens

Every reader of answers (scoring, progress, the questionnaire, the
export) filters with `reducedPillarScopeSQL`. The rollover's `INSERT ...
SELECT` in `rolloverSQL` didn't, so a SaaS-scored system's Devices and
Applications answers were copied into post-anchor cycles where nobody
can see or clear them. Scores stay right, but anything counting raw
`scores` rows counts them, and the next rollover would copy them forward
again.

### The fix

- `rolloverSQL` applies the rule against the target call. The scoring
key and pillar are scalar subqueries rather than joins on the copy's
FROM, so a system with an unmapped or NULL-key environment, or a
function with no question, keeps its answers. On the version-translate
path the rule is judged on the target-version function, the row that
lands.
- The rollover's `expected`/`translatable` counts use the same
predicate, so a normal rollover into a reduced-scope call doesn't fire
`ROLLOVER_ANOMALY`. Skipped rows get their own `ROLLOVER_SCOPE_SKIPPED`
line (deliberately not alarmed), and `ROLLOVER_ANOMALY
reason=scope_hid_all` fires if the rule ever hides every answer, so a
misconfigured rule can't silently empty a cycle.
- Compare Data Calls (`scorediff.go`) leaves out a pillar that is out of
scope for the system in either compared call, on both sides. Without
this, the cleanup (or the next rollover) would make every reduced-scope
system show its excluded pillars as removed.

### The judgment call to look at

In Compare Data Calls I hide a pillar from both sides if it's out of
scope in either call, rather than applying each side's own rule.
Per-side would show every SaaS system's prior-cycle Devices and
Applications answers as removed when comparing the last pre-anchor cycle
with the anchor cycle. Hiding on both sides treats those pillars as "no
longer asked", not "removed". Because the rule only turns on as
deadlines get later, this is the same as judging by the later call. The
cost: a SaaS system whose only differences are on those pillars shows
"No changes" with no hint that two pillars were left out. That's a UI
wording follow-up.

Two known limits, both shared with every other reader and listed as out
of scope on #645: scope follows the system's current environment, and
the rollover decides scope once, at copy time. A system mis-mapped to
SaaS when a call is created and corrected later comes up blank on
Devices and Applications instead of pre-filled; the previous cycle still
holds its answers.

### Cost of the Compare Data Calls change

Unscoped admin diff of the last two annual cycles, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`
against production in a read-only transaction:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| execution, warm cache | 4.29 s | 4.73 s |
| rows returned | 24,864 | 24,586 |

The 278 fewer rows are the hidden carried-forward answers that no longer
show as changes. The scope lookups are LEFT JOINs on primary keys with
one `NOT EXISTS` per side.

### Tests

- New integration tests: rollover into a post-anchor call (excluded
pillars skipped), a pre-anchor call (everything copied), unmapped /
NULL-key environments and a question-less function (nothing dropped),
the translate path, scope following an environment change between
cycles, and a rule that hides every pillar (alarm fires). Compare Data
Calls: post/post, pre/post, pre/pre and NULL-key cases, with a real
change as a control.
- Two existing tests changed because the behavior did:
`TestRolloverTranslatesAcrossVersionsIntegration` now expects 4 fewer
copied rows (its fixture's two SaaS systems have answers on every
pillar), and the `DataCall104` regression bar picks a visible answer for
its one real change.
- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration` and `make test-full`
(Emberfall 327/0) pass. No API shape change, so no OpenAPI or Emberfall
updates.

### Deploy notes

No migration. Nothing changes until an admin creates a data call. After
merge, run the guarded cleanup from #645 so the current cycle's raw rows
match what the app shows.

fix(misc#447): wait for the API before the backend smoke test (#644)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#447

## Impact

The smoke test in Build and Smoke Test has been failing at random, and
when it fails the deploy stops before Terraform runs. On 2026-11-13, 3
of the 6 smoke test runs failed:

- The merge of
[ztmf!642](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/642) passed on
dev and failed on prod
([run](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/actions/runs/43357886394)).
Prod did not deploy, and nothing told us. Prod stayed behind main for
about 17 hours, until the next deploy got through.
- The merge of
[ztmf!640](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/640) failed on
dev, then on prod
([run](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/actions/runs/43497941657)).
Each needed a manual rerun. That deploy carried the renewed TLS cert for
[ztmf#578](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/issues/578), with the
old cert expiring 2026-11-15, so a failure that went unnoticed would
have taken the site down.

Any merge can hit this, including a security fix that needs to reach
prod. A failed prod build leaves prod behind main with no alert, and the
failure looks like 300 broken endpoints, which points whoever reads it
in the wrong direction.

## Cause

The compose step returns as soon as the containers start, and emberfall
runs right after it. The API only listens once its migrations and the
test seed finish, and nothing waited for that. In every failed run, all
requests got `connection refused` within half a second of compose
reporting the services up.

There is a second way to get the same result. The API runs its
migrations before it listens and exits if it cannot reach the database.
The Postgres healthcheck used `pg_isready -U postgres` over the unix
socket, which can pass while the image is still initializing on a
temporary socket-only server, just before it restarts. If the API
connects in that window, it exits and never listens. The job kept no
container logs, so I could not tell which of the two happened. This PR
fixes both and keeps the logs from now on.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/backend.yml`: a Wait for API step between compose
and emberfall. It curls `http://localhost:8080/` until it gets any HTTP
answer, for up to 90 seconds, and fails with a clear message if it never
does. The API image is distroless with no shell or curl, so the check
runs from the runner, which reaches the API over host networking. A new
API and Postgres Logs step runs on failure and prints both containers'

commits.message:
feat(misc#437): add the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor to ECS tasks (#629)

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#437.

Adds the CrowdStrike Falcon container sensor to every ECS Fargate task
definition: the API, the on-demand ops task, and all three containers in
the per-PR preview environments. It is on in dev and impl and off in
prod. With the switch off, the rendered task definitions are identical
to main.

### How it works

Fargate gives no host access, so the sensor runs inside each task. An
init container copies the sensor into a shared volume, and every other
container waits for it, mounts the volume at `/tmp/CrowdStrike`, gets
`SYS_PTRACE`, and starts through the sensor's entrypoint wrapper in
front of its own entrypoint. This is the same shape the CrowdStrike
patching utility and CrowdStrike's `terraform-aws-ecs-fargate` module
produce.

The new `infrastructure/modules/falcon-sensor` module does the wrapping.
I didn't use CrowdStrike's module because it protects one container and
puts the CID in plain environment variables; the preview task has three
containers. I didn't register the patching utility's output either,
because it registers outside Terraform and the next apply would revert
it.

`FALCONCTL_OPTS` (CID, provisioning token, grouping tags) comes from an
SSM SecureString per cluster, `/crowdstrike/falconctl-opts/<cluster>`,
through `secrets`. The ARN is built from the name, so no secret value
lands in Terraform state, the repo, or the task definition. Each
container's original entrypoint and command are set explicitly instead
of left for the sensor to discover. A plan-time check fails if a
container's own `command` or `entryPoint` later drifts from that map, so
dev (on) and prod (off) can't quietly run different commands:

| Container | Wrapped entrypoint ends with | command |
|---|---|---|
| api (shared and preview) | `/usr/local/bin/ztmfapi` | none |
| ops | `/usr/bin/busybox` | `sleep infinity` |
| postgres (preview) | `/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh` |
`postgres` |
| ui (preview) | `/docker-entrypoint.sh` | `nginx -g daemon off;` |

The api row is the one to check: the distroless image has no entrypoint,
so the binary itself becomes the last wrapped element with no command.
That follows CrowdStrike's module for the binary-only case, and it
starts and registers on the preview (see Testing).

### Other changes when enabled

- Task memory: api and ops 512 to 1024, preview 1024 to 2048, as
headroom for the sensor process that now runs inside each container. The
init container finishes before the app containers start, so it isn't the
reason.
- Execution roles get `ssm:GetParameters` on the cluster's parameter,
and the services wait for that grant before rolling.
- The init container logs to the task's existing log group under a
`falcon-init` prefix.
- The ops task security group gets 443 egress to 0.0.0.0/0, like the api
task. Today it only reaches the VPC endpoints, which can't serve the
sensor image or reach the CrowdStrike cloud.

### Riders

- `scripts/db-tunnel.sh` read `containers[0]` for the ECS Exec agent
status and the port-forward target. With the init container in the task,
that slot may not be the ops container, so it now selects the container
by name and fails clearly if it can't find it.
- The deploy-failure diagnostics in `infrastructure.yml` had the same
`containers[0]` assumption; they now list every container by name, like
the preview workflow already does.
- The Lint-Terraform CI job now runs the module's `terraform test`.

### Testing

- `terraform fmt -check`, `tflint` and `terraform validate` pass on both
roots.
- `terraform test` on the new module: 12 passed, now also run in CI. The
init dependency is `SUCCESS`, and the tests fail if it goes back to
`COMPLETE`. It covers the disabled passthrough, wrapping with the real
preview shapes (existing secrets and dependsOn merged, untouched keys
preserved), the init container's fields, and each guard (reserved name,
missing entrypoint, multi-word entrypoint, command drift).
- Rendered both roots at main and at this branch with mock providers:
with the switch off, container definitions, memory and volumes match
main. With it on, every container is wrapped and `FALCONCTL_OPTS`
appears only in `secrets`.
- No Go changes, so no unit, integration or Emberfall runs were needed.
- Reviewed by five independent review passes and a second-opinion
review; findings are fixed in the second commit.
- Ran against the real sensor on this PR's preview, rebuilt from the
merge with main on 2026-11-12. The init container pulled the image and
exited 0, all three containers started, and `falconctl -g --aid` printed
an agent ID in each of `api`, `ui` and `postgres` (sensor 7.40.7903.0).
The image digest pinned in `modules/falcon-sensor/variables.tf` is the
init container's `imageDigest` from that task.
- The 2026-11-02 preview also ran with the sensor on and reached steady
state, so the dev SSM parameter, the image pull and the egress were
already proven there.

### Deploy notes

- The SSM parameters already exist in both accounts. If one is missing,
the tasks on that cluster fail to start.
- On merge, dev gets the sensor. Impl gets it only when the nightly
main-to-impl sync PR is merged. Prod stays off until a follow-up flips
`falcon_enabled` in `prod.tfvars` after the dev sensors are confirmed
connected.
- The app containers wait for the init container to exit 0 (`SUCCESS`).
A broken sensor image or copy now stops the task with the error on
`falcon-init`, instead of starting the app and failing later on a
missing file.
- Watch the first dev deploy after merge. If the sensor can't start
there, the API service never reaches steady state, the dev apply times
out, and the prod job is skipped for that merge and any after it until
dev is fixed, even though prod has the sensor off.
- The ops task is the only wrapped container that runs as nonroot and
has not run under the wrapper yet. Run it once in dev after merge (`make
db-shell-dev`) before relying on it; that and the entrypoint drift gaps
from review are tracked in a follow-up ticket.
- Preview environments default to on, so every preview built after merge
carries the sensor.

### Accepted exposure

`FALCONCTL_OPTS` carries the provisioning token as an environment
variable in each wrapped container, including preview environments
running PR code, so an in-repo PR author could print it. That is
inherent to how the sensor activates (CrowdStrike's own module puts it
in plain `environment`). A provisioning token only enrolls sensors to
our CID.

Release Notes

The most notable changes in this release are:

Breaking Change

  • Upgraded requirement: Go language version is Go 1.26.0 or later, due to upgrading dependency package golang.org/x/crypto

Security
